title: Labs
text: A lab: one bigger problem in a few parts, in a playground, using what the topic taught. Help costs coins.
why: It's where you really use what you've learned, and you can get it wrong without losing anything. It also gives coins a use besides the shop, so studying pays off when you're stuck.
pick: Yes. A lab after a topic's lessons, not locking the test. Hints cost coins; with none, you can still see a part's answer, but it earns nothing.
details:
Your idea, worked out. Here's how I'd make it.

What a lab is. One problem bigger than a lesson's questions, in three to five parts, set in a playground with the parts lessons use (the map, sliders, the answer forms). Each part is marked like a lesson step, so close answers count as close and a wrong one says why. No timer, and you can leave and come back where you were.

An example for the hurricane topic: "Storm season". It's August, and three storms have just formed. Part 1: mark which can grow stronger, from the sea's warmth. Part 2: draw each one's likely path on the map. Part 3: pick which coasts get a warning first. Part 4: one storm turns over cool water. Say what happens to it, and why.

Help. Each part has up to three hints, each costing more coins: a nudge (which idea from the lessons applies), a pointer (the map shows where to look), and the answer. Coins come from lessons, review and labs. A lab done without hints pays the most.

What could go wrong, and what I'd do about it. Coins also buy things for your room, so you might save them and stay stuck rather than spend. So the answer is always reachable: with no coins left, a part can still show its answer, but that part earns nothing. And a lab never blocks the path: the test opens once the lessons are done, lab or no lab, so a hard lab can't hold you up.

Where it sits on the path: animation, lesson, animation, lesson, then the lab, then the test. Facts a lab uses count as reviewed, like any question.

Cost: about 6 to 10 agent-hours for the lab runner, the hints and coins, and one pilot lab. It would come after review, which is being built now. Coins themselves aren't built yet; they'd come with this.
